name: Week 16 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Seated Leg Curl + Calf Raise)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. Squat steps to 80/side, keeping the 6/7/8/8 rep volume — reps stay the progression lever, not heavier load. Leg press steps to 4 plates as the new go-to, with the deep knees-to-chest ROM held as the priority. Spotlights cycle forward to the two lifts due for a refresh — seated leg curl (slow tempo is the stimulus you feel deeply) and the leg-press calf raise (drill the deep heel-drop + slow eccentric at double-leg, single-leg stays gated). Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the two hamstring lifts don't stack. Bulgarian holds its stepped-up load.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Squat steps to 80 / 6-7-8-8 (reps stay the lever); leg press steps to 4 plates, deep ROM held. Leg curl + calf raise get the spotlight refresh — leg curl for the slow-tempo feel, calf raise for the deep heel-drop eccentric. Leg curl before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. The slow tempo is what you feel deeply here. Spotlight drills the ankle-under-pad contact + locked lap pad + full-ROM squeeze at 90, so the hamstring does the work and the lower back stays out of it.

Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. The slow eccentric started biting hard at 3 plates. Spotlight drills the deep heel-drop off the platform edge + the 3-4s eccentric at double-leg — the single-leg conversation waits until the double-leg eccentric is fully dialed.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W13 Bulgarian (NEW) · W14 squat + incline RDL · W15 leg press + Bulgarian · W16 leg curl + calf raise (current) · W17 cycle forward — squat depth + incline RDL refresh.
watchpoints: **Loads** — squat steps to 80/side, leg press 4 plates (ROM first), calf raise 3 plates, leg curl 90, incline RDL 45lb plate, Bulgarian 50lb (optional 60 if easy).

**Squat steps to 80 / 6-7-8-8.** Keep the rep volume — reps are the progression lever, not heavier weight. Let the reps land where they fall at the new load and build them back to 8/8 over the coming weeks; keep the depth.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL.** Reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second — keep the prescribed order.
**Bulgarian holds 50lb** — single DB (suitcase); optional bump to 60 if 50 feels easy. If anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight and finish — the standing rule on this lift.
**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.
Set 1: 45/side x8. Set 2: 70/side x6 — heavy-ish primer before 80. Same depth as the working sets.

**LOAD:** 80/side. 4 sets: **6 / 7 / 8 / 8** — same rep volume as 75; the weight steps up, the reps stay. Reps are your progression lever from here, not heavier load. **Drop the last set (the 4th 8) if it feels heavy or unsteady** — bank 6/7/8 clean rather than grind a shaky 8.
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- 'Spread the floor' — screw the feet into the ground
- Knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing the depth set by set, even as the load steps up
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

**Reflection:** the reps may land a little short of 8/8 on the first session at 80 — that's fine, build them back up over the coming weeks at this weight. Does the depth hold at 80 the way it did at 75? If the bottom shortens to make the number, ease back. Depth + reps, not heavier load.

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side — the new go-to. The deep knees-to-chest ROM still comes first: if 4 plates shortens the ROM or lets the lower back lift off the pad, drop back to 3 plates. ROM is the work; the load follows it.
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** This deep position trains the abs/QL/core more than the quads — that's the intent
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens up once the hips are warm (the warmup + squat before it prime this), so don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off the pad, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**
- **Don't lock out hard at the top** — leave a hair of bend. Breath: in on the descent, out on the drive

sets.name: 🔆 Leg-Press Calf Raise (Spotlight — Same Machine, Stays Right Here)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the deep heel-drop + slow eccentric, drilled:**
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off** — no plate under the foot; the platform edge gives the heel drop
- **Both feet on the platform** — double-leg
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go. That deep stretch is the growth signal
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **3-4s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus, not added load; it started biting hard at 3 plates
- **1s squeeze at the peak**, no bouncing. Breath continuous, don't hold

**Reflection:** does the 3-4s eccentric stay honest (no rushing) at the deep heel-drop for all 3 sets at 3 plates? When the slow double-leg eccentric is fully dialed and starts feeling easy, that's the cue to open the single-leg conversation — not before.

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** single 50lb DB (suitcase) — hold the stepped-up load; optional bump to 60 if 50 feels easy. 3 sets of 8-10 each leg.
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

sets.name: 🔆 Seated Leg Curl (Spotlight — 3 Sets at 90, Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 90. 3 sets of 12, slow tempo.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the slow-tempo feel you get here, drilled clean:**
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus; you feel these deeply when you go slow
- Torso anchored to the seat, no lifting forward; no bouncing out of the bottom

**Reflection:** with the ankle-under-pad contact and the pad locked tight, does the squeeze stay in the hamstring (not the lower back) on the slow eccentric for all 3 sets? This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — take the leg curl fresh.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**
- **At the top:** stop at neutral. Past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this lift works
- Take extra rest between sets if you need it

**Reflection:** where's the stretch landing — hamstrings/glutes (correct) or lower back (too deep / pad placement off)? If lower back, slow down further and check the pad before set 2.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat 4 sets, leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Squat steps to 80 / 6-7-8-8** — keep the reps; reps are the progression lever, not heavier weight.
**Spotlight: seated leg curl + calf raise.** Leg curl drills the slow-tempo feel; calf raise drills the deep heel-drop eccentric at double-leg.
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.
**Bulgarian holds 50lb** — single DB; optional bump to 60 if easy. Drop to bodyweight if anything twitches.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — the tempo is the progression, not the number.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The squat earns a load step (80) while keeping the 6/7/8/8 rep volume — the user prefers adding reps over chasing heavier loads — and the leg press steps to 4 plates with the deep ROM held; the spotlight moves to the two lifts due for a refresh: the leg curl, where slow tempo is the whole feel, and the calf raise, where the deep eccentric has started to bite. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking. Form leads load — building decades, not weeks.
